speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of a high fever and a seizure accompanied by a generalized nonpruritic rash. To begin my assessment, can you tell me exactly how many days have passed since your fever started?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola infantum (Exanthem subitum).

The clinical picture of a high fever (40.5°C) followed by a seizure and then the onset of a generalized, nonpruritic rash in a 9-month-old with up-to-date immunizations is classic for Roseola infantum, caused by Human Herpesvirus 6 or 7. The seizure was likely a simple febrile seizure triggered by the high fever.
